title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE OVERSEAS MIGRATION ACT
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE OVERSEAS MIGRATION ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Overseas Migration Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Persons Subject to Military Service Obligations Whose Overseas Migration Is Restricted, etc.)
(1) “Persons prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as active-duty enlisted personnel or full-time reservists” in Article 3 (2) of the Overseas Migration Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”) means any of the following persons: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2020>
1. Full-time reservists, onboard-ship reservists, social service personnel, arts and sports personnel, technical research personnel or industrial technical personnel under Article 2 (1) 8 through 10, 10-3, 16 or 17 of the Military Service Act;
2. Active-duty enlisted personnel under Article 18 (2) of the Military Service Act (including staff sergeants appointed without volunteering);
3. Conscripted police personnel or obligatory firefighting personnel transferred to service pursuant to Article 25 (1) of the Military Service Act;
4. Alternative service personnel under Article 17 of the Act on Assignment to and Performance of Alternative Service.
(2) “Family members within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 3 (2) of the Act means persons under subparagraph 2 of Article 131 of the Enforcement Decree of the Military Service Act; provided, any of the following persons shall be excluded from family members:
1. Persons aged 60 or older;
2. Persons denied entry under the statutes of the destination country;
3. Persons prohibited from migrating overseas pursuant to Article 3 (1) of the Act;
4. Persons who have already departed for the destination country and acquired permanent residency.
(3) “Persons prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as active-duty commissioned officers or warrant officers” in Article 3 (3) of the Act means the following persons:
1. Active-duty commissioned officers, warrant officers or noncommissioned officers (excluding staff sergeants appointed without volunteering);
2. Public health doctors, public-service advocates, physicians exclusively responsible for military service determination examinations, or public quarantine veterinarians under Article 2 (1) 11 or 13 through 15 of the Military Service Act;
3. Medical officer candidates under Article 58 (2) 1 of the Military Service Act.

Article 3 Deleted. <Nov. 23, 2009>

Article 4 Deleted. <May 27, 1999>

Article 5 (Reports of Overseas Migration)
(1) A person intending to report overseas migration pursuant to Article 6 of the Act shall submit to the Commissioner of the Overseas Koreans Agency a report of overseas migration accompanied by documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; provided, a person who has migrated while abroad under subparagraph 2 of Article 6 of the Act may submit the report to a diplomatic mission under Article 2 of the Act on the Establishment of Overseas Diplomatic Missions of the Republic of Korea (including offices performing consular affairs in areas where no diplomatic mission is established and branch missions or sub-offices under Article 3 of the same Act, but excluding diplomatic missions that do not perform consular affairs or have no consular jurisdiction). <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 19, 2017; Apr. 5, 2023>
(2) In the following cases, the Commissioner of the Overseas Koreans Agency shall issue a certificate of report of overseas migration to a person (hereinafter referred to as a “reporting person”) who has filed a report of overseas migration under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as a “report of overseas migration”), as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs: <Amended on Apr. 23, 2024>
1. Where accepting a report of overseas migration;
2. Where a reporting person applies for issuance of a certificate of report of overseas migration, specifying the purpose of its use.
(3) Deleted. <Apr. 23, 2024>

Article 16 (Registration Requirements, etc.)
(1) A corporation seeking registration of an overseas migration brokerage business under Article 10 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an “overseas migration brokerage business”) shall meet all the following requirements: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2024>
1. Its paid-in capital (meaning basic assets in the case of a nonprofit corporation) shall be at least 100 million won;
2. It shall hold guarantee insurance with an insured amount of at least 300 million won.
(2) A corporation seeking registration of an overseas migration brokerage business shall meet the requirements under paragraph (1) and submit to the Commissioner of the Overseas Koreans Agency an application for registration (including an application in electronic form), accompanied by the following documents (including electronic documents). In such cases, the Commissioner of the Overseas Koreans Agency shall confirm a certified copy of the corporate register through the shared use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. <Amended on May 4, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013; Jan. 5, 2021; Apr. 5, 2023; Apr. 23, 2024>
1. The articles of incorporation;
2. A statement of financial position;
3. A business plan;
4. Documents confirming that the corporation holds guarantee insurance under paragraph (1) 2;
5. A document stating the names and resident registration numbers of its officers.
(3) Where a corporation registered as an overseas migration brokerage business pursuant to paragraph (1) has revenue of at least one billion won for the immediately preceding business year, it shall, notwithstanding paragraph (1) 2, obtain guarantee insurance with an insured amount of at least 500 million won within six months from the last day of the month in which the immediately preceding business year ended.
(4) Matters necessary for the contents of guarantee insurance under paragraphs (1) 2 and (3), the grounds and procedures for insurance claims, etc. shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 19 (Scope of Overseas Migration-Related Duties)
“Duties concerning overseas migration prescribed by Presidential Decree” in Article 10 (1) of the Act means the following duties:
1. Filing reports of overseas migration on behalf of others;
2. Applying for issuance of entry visas for overseas migration on behalf of others;
3. Providing counseling and guidance related to overseas migration;
4. Supporting the settlement of overseas migrants.

Article 19-2 (Processing of Sensitive Information and Personally Identifiable Information)
Where unavoidable for handling any of the following affairs, the Commissioner of the Overseas Koreans Agency may process information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act or materials containing resident registration numbers or passport numbers under Article 19 of the same Decree: <Amended on Apr. 5, 2023; Apr. 23, 2024>
1. Affairs concerning confirmation of migration while abroad under subparagraph 3 of Article 4 of the Act;
2. Affairs concerning reports of overseas migration under Article 6 of the Act;
3. Affairs concerning registration and registration of changes of overseas migration brokerage businesses under Article 10 (1) and (3) of the Act;
4. Affairs concerning confirmation of grounds for disqualification from registration of overseas migration brokerage businesses under Article 10-2 of the Act;
5. Affairs concerning reports of transfer of business under Article 10-3 (1) of the Act;
6. Affairs concerning reports of abandonment of overseas migration under Article 11 of the Act;
7. Affairs concerning reports of permanent return to the Republic of Korea under Article 12 of the Act.

Article 20 (Review of Regulations)
The Commissioner of the Overseas Koreans Agency shall review the appropriateness of the registration requirements, etc. for overseas migration brokerage businesses under Article 16 every three years, using January 1, 2014, as the base date (meaning before January 1 of every third year), and shall take measures such as improvements. <Amended on Apr. 5, 2023>
